chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The women today have innovated a style of combing — one of them deliberately takes the woolly hair braids which the hairdresser weaves together with the hair, then stuffs it with aromatic herbs, then places a thin cloth over it, then sews it with a needle, then places it on her head — then she is afflicted with sexual impurity.

So he said: The women of former times would only comb the front part of their hair. So when the ritual bath (ghusl) befell them due to impurity, instruct her to soak her head thoroughly with water and squeeze it until it is saturated. When it is saturated, there is no problem for her.
He said: I said, 'So what about the menstruating woman?' He said: She must fully undo the hairstyle.

key_terms.الْجَنَابَةُ: Janabah — major ritual impurity caused by sexual intercourse or seminal emission, requiring full-body ghusl (ritual bath)
key_terms.الْحَائِض: A menstruating woman — one in the state of hayd (menstruation), whose obligations during ritual purification differ from those in janabah
key_terms.الْقَرَامِل: Hair braids or extensions made from wool or other materials, used to augment or style hair — a practice that raised jurisprudential questions about water reaching the scalp during ritual bathing
key_terms.الْمَشْطُ: The hairstyle or hair arrangement, including braids and added extensions
key_terms.تُرَوِّيَ: To thoroughly saturate or soak — the key technical criterion for a valid ghusl
key_terms.نَقْضاً: An emphatic verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing the complete and thorough undoing of the hairstyle

ai.seo_question: Does a woman need to undo her braids or hair extensions for ghusl after janabah or menstruation?
ai.summary: Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a contemporary women's hairstyle involving elaborate wool braids sewn into the hair. The Imam distinguished between women of earlier times who braided the front hair simply, and allowed modern women performing ghusl of janabah to simply saturate the hair with water without undoing the elaborate style, provided the water reaches through. However, for the menstruating woman, complete undoing of the braided style is required. This ruling reflects the Imam's practical jurisprudence balancing the obligation of ritual purity with the reality of women's elaborate hairdressing customs.
